newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists want British Labour victory.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists want British Labour victory.

text.p: France's Socialist party said on Wednesday a Labour victory in Thursday's British election would encourage left-wingers in France ahead of their own parliamentary election on May 25-June 1.

"If we could open the month of May with a British Labour victory and end it with the victory of the French Left, it would give an entirely different sense to the European Union," Socialist party spokesman Francois Hollande told reporters.
Hollande said double victories of left-wingers in Britain and France "would create a new balance of power in Europe.

"If we obtained these two results, it would mean we could create a more social Europe, a Europe turned more towards growth and employment. That would also mean that we...could better negotiate transition towards the Euro (single currency)," he said.
"The possible victory of Labour in Britain is an encouragement in our own French and European debate," he said.

"The right in Britain are called Conservatives. Here they are called the RPR (Rally for the Republic) and John Major is cut from the same rightist cloth as (French prime minister) Alain Juppe," said Hollande.
Britain's Labour has a wide lead in opinion polls over the ruling Conservatives, but French Socialists are trailing the ruling centre-right government.
